candidate.quote: The earliest undoubted occurrence of a zero in India is an inscription at Gwalior
candidate.summary: Records the older consensus (quoting an earlier scholar) that the dated Gwalior inscription of 876 CE was the earliest sure Indian zero, with the Bakhshali manuscript 'probably' earlier. Shows how the date of the zero moved.
candidate.limits: Superseded as a dating claim (see the Oxford radiocarbon report). The Gwalior date is a floor for the written zero in India, not evidence of transfer. 1911 work, partly superseded (it knew the Bakhshali manuscript only as 'probably' earlier than Gwalior; dates now debated). OCR text; quote checked against the OCR.

reason: strand_unsupported: the quoted passage dates the earliest Indian zero (Gwalior, 876) and says nothing about transfer to the Islamic world; the strand (India to Islamic world, debated) is not stated by the source. Quote itself verified verbatim in the OCR (Smith & Karpinski 1911). Resubmit without a strand, or with a source that states the transfer.

candidate.quote: The second determination on Folio 16 demonstrated that the initial determination was inaccurate.
candidate.summary: The Oxford report revises the 2017 measurements: folio 16, first dated to the 3rd-4th century and publicised as the oldest zero, was re-measured, and the five-folio model puts production at 799-1102 calCE.
candidate.limits: A report on bark age (terminus post quem), not on when the text was composed; the report itself says the folios may differ in age. It does not discuss routes of transmission. Year not shown on the PDF (a Wikipedia note dates the revision to October 2024).
